# Slippery: every word in the product

*Generated by `node tools/strings.mjs`. Do not edit by hand; edit the
source and regenerate. `npm run verify` fails if this file is out of date.*

## What this is

Slippery is a bet slip tracker. You forward a screenshot of a bet slip to a
Telegram bot **at the moment you place the bet**, and it reads the stake,
odds, selection and bookmaker off the image, watches the game, settles the
bet against a results feed, and shows the real profit and loss on a
calendar. Groups rank friends in units rather than pounds, so a ten pound
bettor and a five hundred pound bettor sit in the same table honestly and
neither learns what the other stakes.

It is for people who already bet and want to know what their record
actually says rather than what they remember. It is not a bookmaker, takes
no bets, and never handles money.

**Four decisions are locked**, because each one cost real money or real
trust to learn:

1. **Capture at placement.** Logging at settlement is what turns a tracker
   into a highlight reel of somebody's winners. It is the only thing here
   nobody else can copy.
2. **The settlement rules.** A wrong grade is worse than no grade, so the
   engine refuses rather than guesses. Ninety minutes only, whole lines
   push, handicaps grade per bookmaker, racing is never automatic.
3. **The iOS constraints.** Every one came from a real device failure:
   16px inputs, 100svh not dvh, at most three backdrop filters, no
   localStorage.
4. **Green means profit and red means loss, always.** Semantic, never
   theme-dependent, which is why there is no green or red theme.

**Stack.** Vanilla JavaScript and CSS built by esbuild into one
self-contained `public/index.html`. Neon serverless Postgres, Vercel
functions, Anthropic for reading slips, Gmail SMTP for codes, and scraped
results feeds. Money is integer pence everywhere and formatted only at the
edge.

## How to read this file

Each section is one screen. Entries appear in the order they appear on the
screen. `(hidden)` marks a state that only shows in certain conditions:
empty states, error messages, loading text. Those are where the wording is
usually worst and hardest to find, which is why they are included.

- text: "Names are permanent so a record always belongs to the same person, and nobody can take a name someone else built a history under."
- accordion question: "Why has the same bet appeared twice?"
- text: "Slippery flags slips that settle identically, such as away goals under 0.5 and BTTS No, and offers to consolidate them so your numbers are not counted twice."

- text: "How the billing works"
- list item: "A paid plan needs a payment method. Choosing one without a usable card leaves the account on the free trial rather than pretending to be subscribed. A promo code that grants free months is the exception, because nothing is charged until those months run out."

## Reference FAQ

- eyebrow: "Reference"
- h1: "Importing and tracking, answered properly."
- sub: "Lists where a list is the honest answer. Prose hides the cases it does not cover."
- accordion question: "Which bookmakers can it read?"
- list item: "bet365"
- list item: "Paddy Power"
- list item: "William Hill"
- list item: "Ladbrokes"
- list item: "Coral"
- list item: "Betfred"
- list item: "Betfair sportsbook"
- list item: "Unibet, LeoVegas and 32Red (one shared format)"
- list item: "Smarkets"
- text: "Anything legible is worth sending. These are the ones real slips have been tested against."
- accordion question: "What can I import?"
- list item: "A screenshot of a slip"
- list item: "A photo of a printed slip"
- list item: "A PDF statement"
- list item: "A CSV export"
- list item: "An Excel export"
- list item: "A screenshot of a profit and loss screen, which lands as dated rows"
- list item: "Pasted text"
- text: "Whatever you drop in, the type is worked out for you. There is no format to pick."
- accordion question: "What columns does a CSV need?"
- list item: "Required: a date, a selection, a stake, and either odds or a return"
- list item: "Optional: bookmaker, market, result, competition, notes, tipster"
- list item: "Money may carry a currency symbol or not"
- list item: "Dates may be day-first or ISO; both are read"
- text: "A row missing a required column is shown to you rather than dropped silently."
- accordion question: "How does duplicate detection work?"
- list item: "A bet is a duplicate when the date, the selection, the stake and the bookmaker all match one you already have"
- list item: "Duplicates are skipped rather than imported, and the import summary says how many and which"
- list item: "The same bet twice inside one file is caught as well as the same file imported twice"
- list item: "If it really was two identical bets, add the second by hand"
- text: "Four fields, all four have to match. Three matching fields is a coincidence, not a duplicate."
- accordion question: "What results can a bet have?"
- list item: "Lost"
- list item: "Void, and the stake comes back with zero profit"
- list item: "Push, where the line landed exactly on the score and the stake comes back"
- list item: "Placed, where the place half of an each way bet landed and the win half did not"
- list item: "Cashed out at a profit"
- list item: "Cashed out at a loss"
- list item: "Cashed out flat"
- list item: "Pending"
- text: "Void and push both return the stake and are tracked separately, because they mean different things about the bet."
- accordion question: "How is profit and loss worked out for each result?"
- list item: "Won: stake × (odds − 1)"
- list item: "Lost: minus the stake"
- list item: "Void or push: zero"
- list item: "Placed: the place half returns at the place price, the win half is lost"
- list item: "Cashed out: the cash out value minus the stake, whatever the game did afterwards"
- list item: "Pending: excluded from profit and loss, counted in pending stake"
- text: "Pending bets never touch your P/L or your ROI. A running bet is not a result."
- accordion question: "How does each way work?"
- list item: "An each way bet is two bets, so a £10 each way is £20 staked"
- list item: "The place half pays at the win price reduced by the place fraction"
- list item: "Place terms are read off the slip, not assumed"
- list item: "Winning gives you both halves; placing gives you the place half only"
- text: "Place terms are read off the slip rather than assumed, because they differ by race and by bookmaker."
- accordion question: "How many slips can I read?"
- list item: "Free trial: two weeks or 35 slips, whichever runs out first"
- list item: "After that: unlimited on either paid plan"
- list item: "A slip the reader gets wrong can be flagged, and the flag refunds the slip"
- text: "Both halves of the trial matter and they run out differently. The dashboard tells you which one is closer."
- accordion question: "What happens to my slip images?"
- list item: "Stored so a bet can be checked against the image it came from"
- list item: "Never shown to anyone else"
- list item: "Deleted when you delete the image, the bet, or the account"
- list item: "Never used to train anything"
- text: "Settings has a one-tap purge for the images alone, which keeps the bets."
- accordion question: "How is my data kept?"
- list item: "Passwords are hashed with scrypt and never stored in a readable form"
- list item: "The session cookie is httpOnly, so no script on the page can read it"
- list item: "Every query is scoped to your account by the database, not by the browser"
- list item: "Slip images sit in the database alongside the bet, not in a public bucket"
- text: "The full processor list, with what each one sees, is on the privacy page."
- accordion question: "Can I get my data out?"
- list item: "CSV, from Settings"
- list item: "JSON, from Settings, with everything including the settlement reasons"
- list item: "Both are the whole ledger, not the current filter"
- text: "Export needs no request and no waiting. It is a button."
- accordion question: "Can I share my record?"
- list item: "A group ranks its members in units, so nobody sees anyone's stakes"
- list item: "Your profile can be public, visible to Slippers you follow back, or private"
- list item: "Nothing is public by default"
- text: "Public tipster pages and password-shared bankrolls are not built. A public leaderboard of gambling returns has a regulatory position that needs answering before it is built, not after."
- accordion question: "What about racing?"
- list item: "Racing bets are logged, tracked and counted"
- list item: "They are never settled automatically"
- list item: "Rule 4, each way terms and starting prices are yours to enter, not ours to guess"
- text: "No results feed we trust publishes finishing positions we can prove, so racing is handed back to you rather than guessed at. That is the same rule the football engine follows."

## Help

- eyebrow: "Help"
- h1: "Common questions."
- accordion question: "Why could a slip not be read?"
- text: "Slippery never guesses at numbers it cannot see, so it asks for a clearer photo. Crop to the slip, avoid glare, and keep the stake, odds and result in frame."
- accordion question: "What does the pace marker mean?"
- text: "The pale line on the target bar shows how far through the period you are. If the green bar is past it, you are ahead of pace."
- accordion question: "What is a unit?"
- text: "A unit is your standard stake, set in Settings. Units let you compare with other people without anyone seeing the money."
- accordion question: "Who can see my numbers?"
- text: "Public means any Slipper who finds you. Friends only means Slippers you follow back. Private means none. Group members always see units of everyone in that group."
- accordion question: "Why can I not change my display name?"
- text: "Names are permanent so a record always belongs to the same person, and nobody can take a name someone else built a history under."
- accordion question: "Why has the same bet appeared twice?"
- text: "Slippery flags slips that settle identically, such as away goals under 0.5 and BTTS No, and offers to consolidate them so your numbers are not counted twice."
- accordion question: "How do I correct a slip Slippery misread?"
- text: "Every field on an uploaded slip is editable before you confirm it, and nothing is saved until you do. A bet already in your ledger can be settled by hand from the running list."

## Terms of use

- button: "Back"
- h1: "Terms of use"
- text: "Draft for review · not yet reviewed by a solicitor"
- text: "Placeholder wording"
- hint: "The structure and the specifics are written against what the code actually does, so nothing here is a blank waiting to be filled in. It still needs a solicitor before launch: the liability cap, the consumer cancellation wording and the jurisdiction clause are the three that carry real risk if they are wrong. The App Store will also require a final version at a public URL."
- h2: "1. Who we are and what this covers"
- text: "Slippery is a bet recording and analytics tool operated from the United Kingdom. These terms cover the website, the installable web app and the Telegram bot @SlipperyAppBot. By creating an account you agree to them."
- h2: "2. What Slippery is not"
- text: "Slippery is not a bookmaker, a betting exchange, a broker or a tipping service. It does not accept bets, hold funds, pay winnings, take a share of a stake or offer advice on what to bet. It holds no Gambling Commission licence because it carries out no licensable activity. Nothing shown in the product is a recommendation to place a bet."
- h2: "3. Age, and what this is for"
- text: "Strictly for adults. Slippery is a tracker for people who already bet. It does not take bets and never handles money. If betting has stopped being fun, free and confidential help is at BeGambleAware.org."
- text: "You must be 18 or over. You confirm this when you create an account. Where we have reason to believe an account holder is under 18 we will suspend the account and delete the data on it."
- h2: "4. Your account"
- list item: "You are responsible for your password and for the link code that connects the Telegram bot to your account."
- list item: "Display names are permanent, so that a betting record always belongs to the same person and nobody can take a name someone else built a history under."
- list item: "One account per person. Accounts may not be shared or transferred."
- h2: "5. The free trial"
- text: "The trial runs for 14 days or 35 slips, whichever runs out first. When it ends, logging new bets stops and everything already logged stays exactly where it is. Nothing is deleted and nothing is held back from export."
- h2: "6. Paid plans, renewal and cancellation"
- list item: "Paid plans renew automatically until cancelled."
- list item: "Cancelling stops the next renewal and keeps access until the end of the period already paid for."
- list item: "UK and EU consumers keep their statutory 14 day cancellation right. Starting to use a paid plan within that period does not remove it, but we may charge for what has been used."
- list item: "Prices may change with at least 30 days notice by email, and a change never applies to a period already paid for."
- text: "Card payments are not yet switched on. The payment screen in the product is a placeholder and takes no card details."
- h2: "7. Automatic reading of slips"
- text: "Slippery reads images of bet slips automatically. It is built to leave a field blank rather than guess at it, and every field is editable before you confirm. A reading may still be wrong. Checking a bet against the slip it came from remains yours to do."
- h2: "8. Automatic settlement"
- text: "Standard football and tennis markets settle themselves against public results sources. The rule the engine follows is that a wrong grade is worse than no grade, so anything it cannot prove is handed back to you rather than settled. Settlement is on the 90 minute score; extra time and penalties never count. Horse racing is never settled automatically."
- text: "Results sources are third parties we do not control and do not pay. They can be wrong, late or unreachable. A figure Slippery displays is a record of what you told it plus what a public source reported, and it is not a statement of what your bookmaker owes you."
- h2: "9. Your content"
- text: "You keep ownership of the slips you upload and the records you create. You give us permission to store and process them only so far as is needed to run the service for you. We do not use your slips or your betting records to train any model."
- h2: "10. Acceptable use"
- list item: "Do not upload slips that are not yours."
- list item: "Do not attempt to read another user's figures, or to work around a privacy setting or a group's unit display."
- list item: "Do not present Slippery output as a verified or audited record when it is not."
- list item: "Do not use automated tools to scrape the service or to place load on it beyond ordinary use."
- list item: "Do not use Slippery to run a paid tipping service without saying plainly that the figures are self reported."
- h2: "11. Groups and rankings"
- text: "Groups rank members in units rather than in money, so nobody learns anyone else's stake size. Joining a group means the other members can see your unit figures for that group. Leaving a group stops that immediately. A group is not a competition with a prize and there is nothing to win in it."
- h2: "12. Taking a break"
- text: "You can stop your own account logging bets for a fixed period. A break is enforced on the server, and it can be extended but never shortened, including by us. That is deliberate: the decision belongs to the version of you that made it."
- h2: "13. Availability"
- text: "We aim to keep the service running and give no uptime guarantee. Maintenance, a failure at a hosting provider or a results source going dark can all interrupt it. Nothing here obliges us to keep any particular feature, results source or integration running."
- h2: "14. Suspension and ending your account"
- text: "You can delete your account at any time from Settings. Deletion removes your bets, your stored slip images, your group memberships and the account itself. We may suspend or close an account that breaks these terms, and where we do we will say why unless the law prevents it."
- h2: "15. Liability"
- text: "Nothing here limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud, or for anything else that cannot lawfully be limited. Subject to that, and to the extent the law allows, the service is provided as it is, and we are not liable for gambling losses, for bets placed or not placed, for a bookmaker settling differently from Slippery, or for indirect or consequential loss. Where liability cannot be excluded it is limited to the amount you have paid us in the previous 12 months."
- h2: "16. Changes to these terms"
- text: "We will give at least 30 days notice by email of a change that materially affects you. Continuing to use the service after a change takes effect means you accept it. If you do not, you can cancel and export everything first."
- h2: "17. Law and getting in touch"
- text: "These terms are governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction. Consumers keep the protection of the mandatory law where they live. Questions go to the support address on the help page."

## Privacy policy

- button: "Back"
- h1: "Privacy policy"
- text: "Draft for review · not yet reviewed by a solicitor"
- text: "Placeholder wording"
- hint: "Every processor named below is one this deployment actually uses, and every retention period is one the code enforces rather than a number chosen to look reasonable. Two things are outstanding and only the owner can close them: ICO registration, which is required before public launch, and confirming the transfer safeguard with each US processor."
- h2: "1. Who is responsible for your data"
- text: "Slippery is the data controller for the personal data described here, under the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Registration with the Information Commissioner's Office is required before public launch and is outstanding."
- h2: "2. What we collect"
- list item: "Account: email address, a hashed password, display name, the date you signed up and whether the email is verified."
- list item: "Betting records: stake, odds, selection, market, bookmaker, competition, result, profit or loss, the date placed and the capture stage."
- list item: "Slip images: photographs, screenshots and PDFs of bet slips and profit screens that you upload or forward."
- list item: "Telegram: your Telegram user id and chat id, only if you link the bot."
- list item: "Preferences: theme, unit size, currency, privacy setting, counting mode and any break you have set."
- list item: "Social: the groups you belong to, the Slippers you follow, and who follows you."
- list item: "Technical: IP address and user agent, held transiently for rate limiting and for keeping the service secure."
- text: "We do not collect your bookmaker login details, your card details, your date of birth, your location or a device identifier."
- h2: "3. Slip images, specifically"
- text: "A slip image is the most sensitive thing we hold. It can show your bookmaker account, your stake, a reference number and sometimes your name. It is sent to an automated reading service to extract the fields, then stored so a bet can be checked against the image it came from. It is never shown to another user and never used to train anything. Settings has a one tap purge that deletes every stored image and keeps the bets."
- h2: "4. Why we process it, and our lawful basis"
- list item: "Running your account and showing you your records: performance of our contract with you."
- list item: "Reading slips and settling bets: performance of our contract with you."
- list item: "Sending a verification code, a password reset and service notices: performance of our contract with you."
- list item: "Keeping the service secure, rate limiting and preventing abuse: our legitimate interests in a working, unabused service."
- list item: "Groups, following and rankings: performance of our contract, and only for the groups you join."
- list item: "Keeping records of payments and cancellations, once payments are live: our legal obligation."
- text: "We do not process your data for advertising and we do not profile you."
- h2: "5. Is a betting record special category data"
- text: "We treat it as sensitive whether or not the law classes it so. It reveals financial behaviour and it can reveal a gambling problem. That is why nothing is public by default, why groups show units rather than money, and why the images have their own purge control."
- h2: "6. Who processes it for us"
- list item: "Neon, Inc. (US and EU) hosts the Postgres database. It holds everything in section 2 except the images sent for reading. neon.tech/privacy-policy"
- list item: "Vercel Inc. (US) hosts the site and the serverless functions. It sees requests in transit, including IP addresses, and holds no betting data at rest. vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy"
- list item: "Anthropic PBC (US) reads slip images and returns the extracted fields. It receives the image and nothing else, no account identifier and no email address. Data sent through the API is not used to train models. anthropic.com/legal/privacy"
- list item: "Google LLC (US) delivers outbound email over Gmail SMTP. It sees the recipient address and the message, which contains a verification or reset code and nothing about your bets. policies.google.com/privacy"
- list item: "Telegram FZ-LLC (UAE) delivers bot messages, only if you link the bot. It sees the messages you send the bot, including any slip image you forward to it. telegram.org/privacy"
- text: "Results sources are read, not sent to. FlashScore, football-data.co.uk, ESPN, SofaScore and football-data.org receive a request for a fixture list and receive nothing about you."
- h2: "7. International transfers"
- text: "Neon, Vercel, Anthropic and Google are United States companies and Telegram is registered in the United Arab Emirates. Transfers rely on the UK International Data Transfer Addendum to the EU Standard Contractual Clauses, or on a UK adequacy decision where one applies. The database region is chosen in the EEA."
- h2: "8. How long we keep it"
- list item: "Slip images: 90 days from upload, then deleted automatically. Sooner if you delete the bet, purge the images or close the account."
- list item: "Betting records: until you delete the bet or close the account."
- list item: "Account details: until you close the account."
- list item: "Verification and reset codes: 10 minutes, then they stop working and are removed."
- list item: "Sessions: 30 days, or until you log out."
- list item: "Rate limiting records: 24 hours."
- list item: "Payment and cancellation records, once payments are live: 6 years, because tax law requires it."
- list item: "Backups: overwritten within 30 days of a deletion."
- h2: "9. What we never do"
- text: "We do not sell your data. We do not share your betting figures with bookmakers, advertisers, credit reference agencies, insurers or employers. We run no advertising network, no analytics product and no third party script on the page."
- h2: "10. What other users can see"
- list item: "Private, the default: nobody sees your figures."
- list item: "Followers: only Slippers you follow back."
- list item: "Public: any signed in Slipper who finds you."
- list item: "Group members always see your unit figures for that group, whatever your setting. They never see your stake size."
- h2: "11. Security"
- list item: "Passwords are hashed with scrypt and are never stored or logged in a readable form."
- list item: "The session cookie is httpOnly, Secure and SameSite, so no script on the page can read it."
- list item: "Every query is scoped to your account by the database rather than by the browser."
- list item: "Slip images sit in the database beside the bet, not in a public bucket with a guessable URL."
- list item: "Secrets are held as environment variables and are never written to a file, a log or a message."
- h2: "12. Cookies and similar technologies"
- table heading: "Technology"
- table heading: "Purpose"
- table heading: "Type"
- text: "Session cookie"
- text: "Keeps you signed in between visits"
- text: "Strictly necessary"
- text: "Theme preference"
- text: "Remembers the colour scheme you chose"
- text: "Service worker cache"
- text: "Serves the app offline and on a slow connection"
- text: "All three are strictly necessary, so no consent banner is required. There is no advertising, analytics or tracking cookie of any kind. Fonts are served from our own domain rather than a font network, so no third party sees your visit."
- h2: "13. Automated decision making"
- text: "Reading a slip and grading a bet are automated. Neither produces a legal or similarly significant effect: a grade changes a number on your own dashboard and can be corrected by you at any time. Nothing about your account, your access or your price is decided automatically."
- h2: "14. Your rights"
- list item: "Access a copy of your data. Export to CSV or JSON is self service in Settings."
- list item: "Correct anything wrong. Every field on a bet is editable."
- list item: "Delete your data. Account deletion is self service and removes bets, images, groups and the account."
- list item: "Restrict or object to processing based on legitimate interests."
- list item: "Portability, in a machine readable format, which the JSON export is."
- list item: "Withdraw consent where processing relies on it, which today is only the Telegram link."
- text: "We answer within one month. There is no charge unless a request is manifestly unfounded or excessive."
- h2: "15. Complaints"
- text: "If we have not got something right, tell us first. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk, or to the supervisory authority where you live."
- h2: "16. Children"
- text: "The service is not for anyone under 18. We do not knowingly collect data from under 18s, and where we learn that we have, we delete it."
- h2: "17. Changes to this policy"
- text: "Material changes are notified by email at least 30 days before they take effect. The date at the top of this page is when it last changed."

## Telegram bot

*Every message the bot can send, from `api/_lib/bot-strings.js`. Placeholders are shown in capitals. Telegram markdown: `*bold*`, `_italic_`.*

- `welcome`: "Welcome to Slippery. Forward me a bet slip the moment you *place* it. I read the stake, odds and selection off the image, watch the game, and settle it into your profit and loss. Capturing at placement is the point: it is what stops a tracker quietly becoming a highlight reel of your winners. To link this chat to your account, open Settings on the site and send me the six character code shown there, like this: /link ABC123 Send a slip whenever you are ready."
- `help`: "*What I do* Send a slip photo and I read it, then ask you to confirm. *Commands* /start, what this bot is /link CODE, connect this chat to your account /whoami, which account this chat is linked to /unlink, disconnect this chat /today, today's profit and loss /pending, bets still running /stop, pause every message from me I never guess at a number I cannot read. If a slip is blurred I will ask for a clearer photo rather than invent a stake."
- `unknownCommand`: "I do not know that one. /help lists what I can do."
- `gotVoice`: "I cannot listen to audio. Send a screenshot of the slip and I will read it."
- `gotSticker`: "Nice. I read bet slips though, so send me a screenshot of one."
- `gotLocation`: "I do not do anything with locations. Send a screenshot of a bet slip instead."
- `gotFile()`: "I cannot read a NAME. Send a screenshot, a photo, or a PDF of the slip."
- `gotTextBet`: "That looks like a bet, but I only log what I can see on a slip. Send the screenshot and I will read the stake and price off it."
- `nudge`: "Send me a *photo or screenshot of a bet slip* and I will read it. Forward it the moment you place the bet, not after it settles, that is the whole point of Slippery. /help for what else I can do."
- `stop`: "Messages paused. Send /start when you want them back. If you want a real break from betting itself, Settings has a break control that locks the app for as long as you choose, and GamCare is on 0808 8020 133."
- `notLinked`: "This chat is not linked to an account, so nothing I read would be saved."
- `notLinkedHow`: "Open Settings on the site, and send me the six character code it shows: /link ABC123 The code lasts ten minutes and you can generate a new one whenever you like."
- `linkNoCode`: "Send /link followed by the code from Settings, like /link ABC123"
- `linkBadShape()`: "That does not look like one of my codes. They are six characters, letters and numbers, with no O, I, or zero in them. You sent: NAME"
- `linkNoMatch`: "That code did not match an account. Codes last ten minutes, so it may have expired. Open Settings and generate a new one."
- `linkExpired`: "That code has expired. They last ten minutes. Open Settings and generate a new one."
- `linkTakenByOther()`: "This chat is already linked to *NAME*. I will not move it without being told to. Send /unlink first if you really want to connect it to a different account."
- `linkAlready()`: "This chat is already linked to *NAME*. Nothing to do."
- `linkUsed`: "That code has already been used. Open Settings and generate a new one."
- `linkAccountElsewhere`: "That account is already linked to a different Telegram chat. Send /unlink from that chat first, or unlink it in Settings."
- `linked()`: "Linked to *NAME*. Send me a slip whenever you are ready."
- `linkNoDb`: "Account linking is not available on this deployment yet."
- `welcomeBack()`: "This chat is linked to *NAME*. Forward me a slip when you place a bet, and I will read it and log it."
- `whoami()`: "This chat is linked to *NAME*, since VALUE. Send /unlink to disconnect it."
- `whoamiNone`: "This chat is not linked to any account."
- `unlinked()`: "Unlinked from *NAME*. I will not save anything sent here until it is linked again. Nothing has been deleted: everything already logged is still on your account."
- `unlinkNone`: "This chat was not linked to anything."
- `reading`: "Reading your slip…"
- `trialOverSlips()`: "That is all NAME free slips used, so I have stopped reading. Subscribe in the app and send it again. Everything logged stays where it is."
- `trialOverDays`: "Your two week trial is over, so I have stopped reading slips. Subscribe in the app and send it again. Everything logged stays where it is."
- `onBreak()`: "You are on a break until NAME, so I am not logging anything. A break can be extended but never shortened, including by me."
- `noReader`: "The slip reader is not switched on for this deployment (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set), so I cannot read that. Nothing was logged."
- `noDatabase`: "This deployment has no database connected (DATABASE_URL is not set), so there is nowhere to save a bet. Nothing was logged."
- `tooFast`: "That is a lot of slips at once. Give me a minute and send the next one."
- `downloadFailed`: "I could not download that image. Try sending it again."
- `tooLarge`: "That image is too large for me to read. Try a screenshot instead."
- `readerFailed()`: "I could not read that one: NAME. Nothing was logged."
- `unreadable`: "*I could not read that slip.* I will not guess at numbers I cannot see. Crop to the slip, avoid glare, and keep the stake, odds and result in frame."
- `slipHeadOk`: "*Slip read.*"
- `slipHeadPartial`: "*Read it, but some fields are missing.*"
- `stageSettled`: "Already settled on the slip."
- `stageInplay`: "In play. I will settle it at full time."
- `stagePrematch`: "Not started. I will settle it at full time."
- `slipMissing()`: "I left NAME blank rather than guess. Tap Edit to fill them in, or send a clearer photo."
- `slipConfirmPrompt`: "Confirm to log it. Nothing is saved until you do."
- `slipNotLinked`: "This chat is not linked, so I cannot log it. Send /link with the code from Settings."
- `notLegible`: "_not legible_"
- `btnConfirm`: "Confirm"
- `btnDiscard`: "Discard"
- `btnEdit`: "Edit"
- `btnRetake`: "Retake"
- `editHow`: "Send the corrected value as a message, for example `stake 25` or `odds 2.10`."
- `retakeHow`: "Send a clearer photo whenever you are ready."
- `callbackDone`: "Done."
- `discarded`: "Discarded. Nothing was logged."
- `draftExpired`: "That reading is more than a day old, so I have let it go. Send the slip again and I will read it fresh."
- `alreadyLogged`: "That one is already logged. I have not added it twice."
- `draftGone`: "That slip has already been dealt with."
- `logNoDb`: "This deployment has no database yet, so I cannot log that."
- `logFailed`: "Something went wrong saving that. Nothing was logged, try again."
- `trialUsedUp()`: "That is all NAME free slips used. Upgrade in the app and send it again."
- `loggedSettled()`: "Logged as *NAME*, VALUE. Today: *THIRD* across FOURTH settled bets."
- `loggedPending`: "Logged. It is on your calendar now, and I will settle it when the game finishes."
- `todayNone`: "Nothing settled today yet."
- `today()`: "Today: *NAME* across VALUE settled bets."
- `pendingNone`: "Nothing running right now."
- `pendingHead()`: "*NAME running*, VALUE at risk"
- `pendingRow()`: "· NAME, VALUE at THIRD"
- `noDbForAccount`: "That needs an account, and this deployment has no database yet."
